summary: CORRECTION (chaos-injector, Gate 5, verified against server.cpp:4160-4182/pg_pool.hpp:84-89): the 'no statement_timeout at all' framing was imprecise -- pg_pool_ is constructed with PgPool::Options' DEFAULT statement_timeout_ms=30000, injected as a startup GUC on every connection. However 30s is a pool-WIDE default, not tuned for this hot path, and vastly exceeds the 1500ms kReadTimeout acquire-budget other callers wait on -- so under concurrency a worker/connection can still be pinned ~20x longer than the caller's own timeout budget, starving the pool shared with RbacStore's fail-closed auth (execution_tracker_ and rbac_store_ share the SAME pg_pool_ singleton per server.cpp:5629/5929, confirmed empirically -- blast radius is fleet-wide auth degradation, not execution-history-only). Recommend: a per-call-site SET LOCAL statement_timeout tuned closer to the caller's own budget, PLUS the index.

summary: Fixed in c27b612e9, per sre's own proposed fix shape from Gate 8 round 3 (row 32/proc-2146-a2r1-gate8-round2-closed-with-open-blocking's summary): a fast-fail-on-saturation primitive at the shared pg_pool.hpp chokepoint. PgPool::try_acquire_for (server/core/src/pg/pg_pool.cpp) now checks, once, at entry, whether the pool is already saturated (idle_.empty() && open_ + connecting_ >= size_ -- the exact condition its own wait loop already requires before it would ever block) and, if so, clamps the wait to min(caller's timeout, Options::saturated_fast_fail) (default 500ms) instead of the caller's full requested timeout. with_txn_for acquires through try_acquire_for so get_children_checked inherits the fix without its own change; get_execution_checked's 5 call sites and every other pg_pool caller in the codebase benefit automatically, per the finding's own framing as a shared-chokepoint issue. The unbounded acquire()/with_txn() (construction-only) and a caller arriving BEFORE saturation are both unaffected -- verified by the full existing test_pg_pool.cpp suite plus the execution_tracker suite passing unchanged. Genuine red/green proof: a new test_pg_pool.cpp case (PgPool try_acquire_for fails fast once already saturated...) saturates a size-1 pool then asserts try_acquire_for(3000ms) returns in well under 1500ms; with the clamp temporarily disabled it failed at ~3000ms (the full timeout), restored it passes at ~500ms (the clamp ceiling). The 500ms default (not a smaller near-zero value) was chosen after auditing every existing try_acquire_for/with_txn_for timeout constant in server/core/src: it sits above every deliberately-short one already in the codebase (largest audited: 500ms), specifically so it does not undercut auth_db.cpp's #2396 login-resilience retry (kAcquireRetryTimeout=150ms), which a prior Gate 4 review (UP-3) had already tuned against being narrowed for exactly this reason. docs/adr/0012-server-postgres-store-contract.md and docs/postgres-store-playbook.md were each given a short update/note so rule 2(a)'s existing 'bound the wait' language is not read as contradicted by the new clamp. Confirmed unaffected: check-api-parity.py, check-mcp-retry-hints.py, and the pg-shard-partition invariant (no new [pg-smoke] case added -- deliberately, since docs/ci-architecture.md documents that set as hand-picked with no new test bodies; the new case is tagged [pg][pool] and lands in its ordinary [pg] shard instead, verified via check-pg-shard-partition.py).
